outcomes.title: Present simple -s/-es after he/she/it
outcomes.objective: Add -s or -es to the verb after he, she or it in present simple sentences about routines.
prerequisites: Knows the pronouns he, she and it

misconceptions.description: The verb is the same for every person
misconceptions.exampleWrong: She go to school at seven.

misconceptions.description: Adds -s to the wrong word or doubles it
misconceptions.exampleWrong: She goes to schools at seven. / He gos.

teachingSuccessCriteria: Adds -s/-es to the main verb after he/she/it

lesson.title: My daily routine
lesson.objective: Describe a daily routine with the present simple.

objectives: Describe a daily routine with the present simple
successCriteria: Uses -es after ch, sh, s, x, o
examples: She gets up at six every day.
My brother goes to work by bus.

items.prompt: Correct the verb: "My mother cook dinner every evening."
Correct the verb: "He teach English at a school."

outcomes.studyNotes: In the present simple we talk about things we do every day. With I, you, we and they the verb stays the same: I get up at six. With he, she and it we add -s: She gets up at six. If the verb ends in -ch, -sh, -s, -x or -o we add -es: He watches TV. She goes to work.

scriptedTutor.explanation: In the present simple the verb changes with he, she and it. We add -s, or -es after ch, sh, s, x and o.
hints: Look at the subject. Is it he, she or it?
With he, she or it, the verb needs an ending.
scriptedTutor.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. Look at the end of the verb.
scriptedTutor.closing: Good work. Remember: he, she, it takes -s or -es.
